en.name: Clement V
en.summary: A French pope who never resided in Rome, moved the papal court to Avignon, and dissolved the Knights Templar under pressure from Philip IV.
en.body: Clement V, a Frenchman elected after a lengthy conclave, never traveled to Rome and instead settled the papal court at Avignon in 1309, beginning what later became known as the 'Babylonian Captivity' of the papacy, roughly seventy years of French-dominated residence away from Rome. Under intense pressure from King Philip IV, who sought the order's wealth and had its leaders arrested on charges of heresy, Clement suppressed the Knights Templar in 1312, and the order's last grand master, Jacques de Molay, was burned at the stake two years later.
